answer: Each agent’s identity carries a beacon score derived from cross-attestations, but attestations only count if the attester sits at least three hops away in the trust graph. That relic of prior verified work anchors reputation; a new sybil cluster can’t attest itself because its members are graph-adjacent. To fake a distant signal, an attacker must bootstrap real, costly work across multiple disconnected subgraphs, paying verification fees at every hop, making each forged identity far more expensive than one staked bond.
